headline: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
summary: Huntress researchers break down how EvilTokens, Knight Office, and Kali365 capture and replay M365 tokens, plus how defenders can detect and contain them.
whyItMatters: These kits enable attackers to hijack Microsoft 365 sessions and access corporate data.
recommendedAction: Implement token monitoring and enforce MFA for Microsoft 365.

headline: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
summary: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version (SHA pinning) is a defense against supply‑chain attacks, but attackers bypassed it in the March 2026 hijack of the Trivy security scanner.
whyItMatters: Bypassing SHA pinning reopens the software supply‑chain attack surface for many projects.
recommendedAction: Update CI pipelines to add additional integrity checks beyond SHA pinning.

headline: Researchers Detail iPhone Flaw That Let Apps Record Audio Despite Denied Microphone Permission
summary: A now‑patched flaw in Apple’s audio service let iPhone and iPad apps record audio after the user denied microphone permission; the fix was released on August 17.
whyItMatters: The vulnerability could have enabled covert audio surveillance on iOS devices.
recommendedAction: Ensure devices run the latest iOS version with the August 17 security update.

headline: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
summary: Operation ShadowCloud, an intrusion campaign targeting government sectors in Asia and Africa, uses undocumented GitDoor and GraphDoor backdoors that leverage Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for covert command‑and‑control.
whyItMatters: Legitimate cloud services are being abused for stealthy C2 communication.
recommendedAction: Audit SharePoint and GitHub activity for anomalous traffic.

headline: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
summary: Ride‑hailing company Uber is notifying nearly 150,000 drivers that attackers stole their data after breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks in early October.
whyItMatters: Driver personal data exposure could lead to phishing and fraud attacks.
recommendedAction: Advise affected drivers to monitor accounts and enable security alerts.

headline: Ransomware affiliate suspect extradited to US, faces 27 years in prison
summary: A Kazakh national was extradited from Italy to the US to face charges for ransomware attacks on schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities, facing up to 27 years in prison.
whyItMatters: The extradition underscores international enforcement against ransomware operations.
recommendedAction: Strengthen ransomware detection and response capabilities.

headline: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
summary: Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.
whyItMatters: Remote lock can protect data on lost devices while preserving user data.
recommendedAction: Evaluate the feature in pilot deployments and update device‑lock policies.

headline: Apple Tightens macOS App Permissions to Limit Data Access Amid AI Agent Security Risks
summary: Apple introduced new macOS controls in the 27.3 beta that give users granular data‑access permissions for apps, including AI agents, via Device Control, Data Access, and Full Disk Access APIs.
whyItMatters: Enhanced permissions reduce the risk of unauthorized data collection by apps.
recommendedAction: Review and adjust app permissions after the beta is released.

headline: Flipper Devices launches $399 ‘Flipper One’ Linux-based multi-tool
summary: Flipper Devices has launched a crowdfunding campaign for Flipper One, a portable Linux computer and networking multi‑tool.
whyItMatters: It provides a new Linux‑based multi‑tool for security researchers.
recommendedAction: Monitor its release for potential security testing use.

headline: Court clears brothers of $25 million Ethereum crypto heist charges
summary: US District Judge Jessica Clarke acquitted two brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency through a scheme that exploited a bug in the Ethereum blockchain.
whyItMatters: The case highlights legal outcomes for large‑scale crypto exploits and the need for continued scrutiny of blockchain bugs.
recommendedAction: Monitor regulatory developments around blockchain vulnerabilities.
